tools.name: read_mandarin
tools.description: Open an interactive reader for a Mandarin article excerpt, message or subtitle passage the user supplies. Hover or tap words for meaning in context, pinyin, parts and uncertainty. Keeps the original text; anonymous and does not save it. Use inspect_mandarin_word for one specific word. Does not fetch

tools.name: inspect_mandarin_word
tools.description: Inspect the Mandarin word or pattern at a Unicode code-point offset in the exact supplied passage. Returns MTW’s contextual word card with expected pinyin, meaning status, parts and offered alternatives. Count Unicode code points, not UTF-16 units; preserve the original passage. A null card means no

tools.name: get_mandarin_account
tools.description: Show the connected MTW account before saving. Requires account connection; reads only the account name and email. Does not list private passages or saved words.

tools.name: save_mandarin_word
tools.description: Save one word from the exact supplied passage to the connected MTW Backpack ONLY when the learner explicitly asks to save it. Re-inspects the word through MTW; for an ambiguous meaning, pass only the sense ID the learner selected from the offered choices. Preserve text, context and title. Use one op

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_mandarin, get_mandarin_account · Private data: get_mandarin_account · Public sink: get_mandarin_account.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_mandarin, get_mandarin_account · Private data: get_mandarin_account · Public sink: get_mandarin_account

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
